Commentary.Commentary: We had great fun covering every single game and hope you did as well. We hope you join us for future games as we really enjoy your company. Till then, this is goodbye and we hope you take care of yourselves.

It began with Sri Lanka whitewashing Australia in the 3-match Test series. Then we witnessed the visitors salvaging their wounded pride by making a terrific comeback in the ODIs with a thumping 4-1 win. And now, we saw the Aussies clean sweeping the T20I series 2-0. Everything in between was as gripping as it could be.

Across all formats, it was nothing short of entertaining. It kept us at the edge of our seats, reeled people in to glue their eyes to the television, pick their phones up and consistently engage in fantasy leagues. These encounters packed a real punch.

So, with this, we have come to an end to Australia's long and gruelling tour in Sri Lanka. This spells the end of Tillakaratne Dilshan's illustrious career in international cricket and it's one he can be proud of. He bows out of the great game with his head held high.

Triumphant Australian skipper DAVID WARNER says  that it has been a fantastic experience that his squad has played fantastic. Jokes a bit about losing the toss and then says that winning the series' is a massive achievement for the ODI team. Adds that they are the highest ranking team in the world and that the boys came with high expectation. They wanted the win on Lankan soil and got it. He ends by saying that he loves Sri Lanka and playing here and that he is thankful to Australia's supporters for coming to support the side and the opponents as well.

Sri Lankan captain DINESH CHANDIMAL says that he is disappointed with the batting and that they were short by 20-25 runs. Credits the Australian bowlers and adds that his side has some homework to do. He opines that Angelo Mathews is a big fish for the squad and that they couldn't find enough balance. There were a lot of youngsters on his side so they can take the positives from it. Says that it is not easy to perform all the time. Ends by thanking Dilshan and says that he is a legend, a match-winner and game changer.

TILLAKARATNE DILSHAN gives thanks to the Australian team. Adds that they lost the Test series 3-0 but came back strongly in the ODI and T20I series. Wishes them the best of luck for the future. (Roshan Abeysinghe translates his speech in Sinhalese) He thanks all the people responsible for his growth, including members of the Sri Lanka Cricket board and his family members.

Man of the Match and Series GLENN MAXWELL says that it got a bit close at the end but he enjoyed it. He adds that it was pretty incredible to lead Australia to their record 263-run score at Pallekele. (On equaling the fastest Australian T20I fifty record) He says that he is normally a record man and is aiming for Aaron Finch's record next. He is glad to be back playing, striking the ball well, hitting cleanly and finding the gaps. He enjoyed playing on the wicket and appreciates the crowd, considering Sri Lanka a good place to play. Adds that the T20 players have enjoyed it here despite not spending as much time. He has not decided on anything and will go back home and do his part at the Matador Cup and Sheffield Shield.

The hosts were not as impressive in the first innings though. They could not put up as high a total as desired with only Dhananjaya de Silva batting exceptionally well. The Australians distinguished themselves with the ball, with Zampa and Faulkner taking 3 wickets apiece.

Sri Lanka owe their second innings success partly to their bowlers who forced the batsmen into difficult positions and to the timid batting from the visitors. The bowlers were ineffectual against the openers but really came into their own when the openers departed. Tillakaratne Dilshan was fantastic with the ball, taking a couple of wickets. Sachith Pathirana stood out as well even though he went for more runs.

It looked like the match was clearly going in favour of Australia but with the dismissal of their openers, their batsmen started folding like a house of cards. It actually looked like Sri Lanka had a chance at one point but the lower-middle order dragged their side kicking and screaming over the finish line to clinch the series.

That's a clean sweep of the series! The Aussies will heave a huge sigh of relief to see the end of that one. Once again, the credit for this win lies in the hands of a couple of very capable batsmen. Maxwell was once again the star amongst the batsmen with a blazing 66 in 29 balls. He was partnered by skipper David Warner and together, their 93-run partnership sealed the win for the tourists.

SIX! DROPPED! Served outside off, Travis comes forward and slogs it through mid-wicket. The ball flies through mid-wicket and flies off Senanayake's hands for a maximum. Travis Head has finally ended the match and that too with a bang! AUSTRALIA WIN THE MATCH BY 4 WICKETS AND 13 BALLS TO SPARE!
Landed outside off, Travis looks to come down and misses his shot.
Straight and outside off, Head looks to slog it but misses and the ball strikes his pads.
Floated on off, Nevill gets into position and paddle sweeps it over the keeper. The batsmen run hard between the wickets and get a triple.
Fullish delivery on the stumps, driven through mid on for a single.
PATHIRANA is the new bowler.
PETER NEVILL is the next batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT! That was the wrong choice of shot for that ball. Pitched outside leg, Wade goes for a pre-meditated reverse sweep and lobs it straight to Dinesh Chandimal at short extra cover who starts celebrating even before he catches it.
Loopy ball on middle and off, defended behind the line of the delivery.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Wade has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Served on off, Wade looks to defend it but edges it to third man for a couple.
Shortish ball outside off, punched through the off side.
Pitched outside off, played to point.
Loopy and full on off, driven to mid on.
Flighted and very slow ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Short on off, cut through point for a single.
Loopy ball outside off, Head looks to punch it away but gets a thick inside edge which just misses the leg stump. Travis Head gets off the mark with a single.
Floated on off, worked to square leg for a single.
SENANAYAKE to bowl.
TRAVIS HEAD is the new man in.

OUT! DILSHAN WITH A WICKET! Excellent stuff. On his final match, he couldn't deliver with the bat but is doing so now with the ball. A flatter ball which is drifting in, Usman Khawaja kneels down to sweep this away but misses the ball completely. Is rapped on the pads and there are roaring appeals for a leg before. The umpire doesn't hesitate to raise his finger and correctly so, because that was dead plumb. Something to smile about for Dilshan.
Bowls it slower through the air, gives it some decent air, Wade gets down and reverse sweeps it square on the off side for a run.
Short and on middle and leg, Usman Khawaja has all the time in the world to rock back and pull it through mid-wicket. Gets a single for it.
Short and flat outside off, Matthew goes back and cuts it through covers for one run.
Drifting in on the pads, Usman sweeps it to short fine leg and runs to the other end for a single. There is a shy at the bowler's end but that misses. One run completed.
Comes from around the wicket, pushes it quicker through the air and well outside off, Khawaja looks to drag the sweep through mid-wicket but fails to do so.
TILLAKARATNE DILSHAN comes into the attack.
Shortish ball outside off, pushed to the covers for a single.
Full delivery on the stumps, driven back to the bowler.
Flighted on middle and leg, swept through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Shortish ball outside off, Wade cuts it to the off side for a single.
Loopy delivery on off, Wade attempts a reverse sweep but misses.
DHANANJAYA DE SILVA is back on. Slip in position.
This time Matthew Wade sweeps it away to deep backward square leg for a single.
Looped up on middle and leg, Khawaja brings out the sweep shot and plays it to deep backward square leg for one.

Not out! Tossed up on middle and off, Khawaja kneels down and looks to sweep this away. Gets it off the inside edge as the ball goes behind to leg slip. Dilshan takes the catch and thinks that the ball has come off Usman's boot. So he asks the umpire to refer it upstairs. Replays show that the ball hit the ground and not the boot.
An appeal for a catch against Khawaja is referred upstairs.
Landed outside off and turning in,  there is a big appeal as Khawaja is struck on the thigh-pad.
Tossed up ball, Usman got into position early and reverse swept that one.
BEATEN! Flatter ball outside off, Khawaja looks to defend it but the ball beats his bat's outside edge.
The batsman rocks onto the backfoot and punches the ball.
Tossed up on off, swept through the leg side for a couple.
BEATEN! Slowish ball on off, Wade looks to sweep but is beaten by the turn and is hit on the pads.
Flighted ball around off, driven through mid on.
Loopy ball outside off, swept through the leg side for a single.
Floated on leg, flicked to the leg side for a single.
DROPPED! Floated around off, turning away, the ball takes the outside edge and goes on the rebound off the keeper's pads.
DROPPED! Tossed up on off, Khawaja drives it back to the bowler. Prasanna leans forward and makes a good stop. The replays show that the ball was actually a catch and that he had dropped it.
USMAN KHAWAJA walks in next.

OUT! FAULKNER IS RUN OUT! What's happening? Australia are suddenly losing wickets and this one looks unnecessary. On the pads, Wade flicks it to mid-wicket and the batsmen decide to take a run. Chandimal fielding there collects the ball and throws it at the striker's end where Faulkner tries to make it to the other end. Replays confirm the Australian all-rounder falls short and Sri Lanka sneak through another wicket.
Full around off, Wade defends it from within his crease.
Full on the pads, Wade sweeps it towards the backward square leg fielder. The Sri Lankans appeal as they think that's out LBW but the umpire shakes his head.
On the pads, Wade works it to the leg side.

NOT OUT! Turn and bounce! Tossed up outside off, Faulkner looks play it but is beaten by the turn. The keeper sees that he steps forward and upsets the bails. The umpire refers the wicket upstairs and the replays show that his foot was comfortably in the crease.
The umpire has referred a stumping decision upstairs.
A similar ball and Wade gets his sweep this time. The ball rides up his forearm and goes fine down the leg side for a single.
BEATEN! Tossed up around off, Wade looks to sweep, misses and is hit on the pads.
MATTHEW WADE is the next batsman in.

OUT! THREE DOWN! The skipper walks off! Flighted on middle, Warner gets down on one knee and half sweep and half pulls it through backward square leg. The ball just doesn't have enough steam and flies into the reverse cup of Thisara Perera. Second wicket in the space of three deliveries!
Full around off, Faulkner defends it off the front foot for a single.
JAMES FAULKNER walks in next.

OUT! STUMPED! Henriques steps down the track and tries to play this one but misses it. The keeper Perera collects the ball and whips off the bails as Henriques tries to make it back. Replays show Moises is just short and he has to walk back. Horror tour for the New South Wales all-rounder.
SACHITH PATHIRANA is back on.
Full on off, looks to defend it but edges it finely to third man for a couple.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone. The umpire has signalled a wide.
Shortish outside off, punched off the back foot through the covers for a single.
Fullish delivery outside off, driven through the covers.
MOISES HENRIQUES is the new man in.

OUT! BOWLED! Tossed up around off, Maxwell waits for it looking to punch it but the ball turns in more than anticipated and Maxi inside edges it onto his stumps. The bowler says something to Maxwell as he walks off and the batsman has something to say back but nothing can cast a shadow over that power-packed innings.
Swing and a miss! Served outside off, Maxwell looks to slash at it but is beaten.
Flighted on leg, nudged down the leg side for a single.
Tossed up on the pads, flicked down the leg side for a couple.
Landed outside off, Warner lofts it over mid off for a single.
Tossed up full toss outside off, Maxwell looks to paddle that delivery but the ball takes an inside edge to the leg side for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. Two runs added to the total.
Floated across the batsman, whipped through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side for a single.
Dhananjaya de Silva to bowl.
Shortish outside off, Maxwell tries to cut but gets a bottom edge to the off side. Single taken to end the over.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
FOUR! Another fine shot! Around off, Maxwell gets into the position and reverse sweeps it through backward point for another boundary.
Short of a length ball on off, Warner pulls it through the leg side for a single again.
On middle and leg, Maxwell sweeps it through square leg for a single.
TWO WIDES! Down the leg side, Warner still goes after it but misses. The keeper fails to collect the ball and the batsmen take an extra run as well.
In the corridor outside off, Warner fails to put his bat on the ball.
SEEKKUGE PRASANNA is introduced now.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Maxwell slaps it and the ball just beats the short third man fielder. Yet another boundary for Maxwell.
3rd T20I fifty for Glenn Maxwell!

FOUR! FIFTY! Glenn Maxwell drills it hard through mid off and gets another boundary. That brings up his fifty as well. This is also the FASTEST FIFTY FOR AN AUSTRALIAN in this format! What a knock so far. Couple of days back he smashed 145 off 65 balls and today as well he's going after the bowlers.
FOUR! Fuller length ball outside off, Maxwell lofts it over the mid off fielder for a boundary this time. The fielder tried his best but it was over him.
SIX! That's another biggie for Maxi! Perera bangs in a short ball on middle and leg, Maxwell quickly goes onto his back foot and pulls it over the long leg region for a biggie all the way.
Short of a length ball on off, Warner slams it through mid on for a single.
Landed outside off, Warner tries to play it to the off side but fails to put his bat on the ball.
THISARA PERERA into the attack.

SIX! POWERFULLY DONE! Landed around off, Maxwell gets down on one knee and sweeps it through backward square leg. The ball doesn't pick up much height but Maxwell has connected very well and it goes well into the crowd for a maximum.

Tossed up on middle and leg, Maxwell swivels in  place and reverse sweeps it. The ball goes very high up but falls short of the ropes at cover and doesn't roll further. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Back of a length ball on middle, punched through mid off for a single.
Around the wicket and on leg, the ball follows Maxwell and he whips it through mid-wicket for a single.
SIX! CLOBBERED! Full outside off, Maxwell steps forward and lofts it. The one is a huge strike and flies all the way into the stands for a maximum.
FOUR! DOWN THE TRACK! Fullish ball on off, Maxwell charges forward and slogs it down the ground for a boundary.
SENANAYAKE is back on.
Fullish ball on middle, punched off the back foot.
Full outside off, played to mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! LOVELY SHOT! Full outside off, Maxwell picks his spot and drives it through the covers to the boundary.
A similar delivery and Maxwell reverse sweeps it again and the ball goes through the covers.
SIX! REVERSE SWEPT! Floated on middle and leg, Maxwell goes for the reverse sweep and the ball sails through the air and falls past the cover fence for a maximum.
Tossed up on leg, Maxwell looks to play it but is struck on the thigh pad.
SACHITH PATHIRANA comes into the attack.
Short outside off, Warner plays the square cut.
FOUR! Full outside off, driven through the covers. The ball flies low and just skims over the fielder at the covers and skips to the boundary.
Length ball on leg, pushed to the covers. The batsmen look to take a single but are sent back by a throw at the striker's end.
Length ball on middle, worked to the leg side for a single.
Down the leg side, Maxwell looks to play it but misses. The umpire has signalled a wide.

Nearly a catch! Short ball on off, Warner looks to leap and play the upper cut but the ball takes a thick top edge. It flies over the keeper to fine leg. The keeper makes a desperate run and then a diving catch but isn't able to secure it. Three runs added to the total. It was a very difficult catch but the keeper gave it his best shot.
FOUR! SLICED! Fullish ball outside off, driven through the gap in the covers for a boundary.

Big appeal for an LBW! On the pads, Warner tries to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. The umpire turns down the appeal and the batsmen sneak through a leg bye. That looked close actually. Replays show the ball would have clipped the leg stump and would have been umpire's call.
FOUR! That's a top shot! Landed outside off, Warner gets into position and goes for the reverse sweep. Beats the fielder at backward point and gets a boundary.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Around off, Maxwell goes for the reverse sweep but misses.
FOUR! BANG! Tossed up on middle and off, Maxwell stands his ground and lofts it over mid on for a boundary.

NOT OUT! Nicely tossed up ball outside off, Maxwell stays in his crease and tries to defend but misses it completely. The keeper whips off the bails and appeals for a stumping. The Sri Lankans look confident and the square leg umpire refers it upstairs. Replays show Maxwell's foot was never raised.
SACHITHRA SENANAYAKE to bowl from the other end and we have a stumping appeal straightaway against Maxwell.
Good length ball around off, the Aussie skipper punches it towards cover-point. Dot ball to end an eventful over.
Lakmal keeps attacking the stumps, David Warner hits this towards backward point.
On a good length and angled across, it's played to the point region for no run.

Whoa! That was intense. Warner seems really ticked off with that. Has every right to as well. Lakmal fires in a yorker on middle and leg, David Warner just about manages to squeeze it out towards Lakmal. He picks it up and showing some aggression, throws the ball at the striker's end. He ends up hitting Warner on the hamstring and he's furious at that. The Lankan pacer quickly raises his hand to apologize. It's turned on here, folks!
PLAY AND A MISS! Slightly fuller in length and well outside off, Warner goes after this one hard but misses it completely.

He's straightaway off the mark. Length ball coming in a touch on off stump, Warner opens the face of the bat and punches it past point. Runs hard and as a result, is comfortably able to come back for the second.
We are back for the chase. It will be the Aussie skipper David Warner to open with Glenn Maxwell partnering him. Suranga Lakmal will lead the Lankan bowling charge. Let's go...
